questions.q: What is this course's throughline, across all 22 lessons?
options: Taking Azure resources you already knew how to click through in a Portal, and learning to describe them as reviewable, repeatable, rebuildable code instead
Teaching what a Storage Account, Fabric Capacity, or Event Hub is from scratch
Replacing the need for the Azure Portal entirely
Teaching a brand-new cloud provider unrelated to Azure
questions.explain: This course never re-taught what any Azure resource is — only how to provision resources you already knew as reviewable, repeatable code.

questions.q: What did the capstone project (Lesson 21) actually prove, according to this lesson?
options: That the earlier 20 lessons' techniques actually compose into a real, working platform's infrastructure — not new material on its own
That Terraform and Bicep cannot be used together in the same project
That modules should never be used for real infrastructure
That remote state is unnecessary for a real capstone project
questions.explain: The capstone is proof the earlier material works together, the same purpose a capstone serves throughout this catalog.

questions.q: Does finishing this course complete the entire Azure/Fabric Data Engineer career path's Advanced stage?
options: No — it closes the provision-it-as-code skill itself, but Kafka is still ahead in that same Advanced stage
Yes — every course in every stage of the path is now complete
No — Git/GitHub/CI-CD and Airflow still need to be built after this
This course has no relationship to the Azure/Fabric Data Engineer path at all
questions.explain: Git/CI-CD and Airflow were already built before this course; Kafka remains as the one course still ahead in the Advanced stage.

questions.q: What structure does this lesson suggest for presenting the capstone in an interview?
options: The same project-story structure from Career & Capstone Lesson 80 — situation, design decisions, trade-offs, what you'd change — applied to IaC-specific decisions
Reciting the entire Terraform configuration line by line with no explanation
Only mentioning that the project used Bicep, without any other detail
There is no recommended structure — improvise entirely
questions.explain: IaC-specific decisions worth naming out loud include why a module was used, why remote state was set up from the start, and why the plan output mattered.

questions.q: Why does this lesson have no "Check yourself" question, unlike every other lesson in the course?
options: There's no next lesson in this course — readiness is instead being able to explain the capstone's own resource blocks to someone else
This lesson was left unfinished on purpose
Check-yourself questions are only used in Chapter 1
The quiz below replaces the need for any written guide content
questions.explain: Every other lesson's "Check yourself" question checks readiness for the next lesson — the finale has no next lesson to prepare for.
